pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2965432100 — High OOM rate on hosted runtime kv-cache nodes (sev=P1). Auto-triggered by >50 OOMs in 5m across r-hosted-*. PagerDuty: https://pd.example/incidents/INC2965432100

sanjay: I'm on it — eng-runtime oncall. Initial alert shows spike at 09:12 UTC, memory pressure on kvcache process. Dumping heap and metric slices now.

maria: Seeing a big jump in kvmap size for a handful of sessions, growth looks linear per-token. Many requests have extremely long prompt prefixes (hundreds of thousands of tokens).

leo: Correlating with canary rollout 2026-03-14 08:50 that toggled continuous-batching v2 and prefetch heuristics. Metric diff: prefetch hit rate +300%, batch-window avg +40ms, avg kv entries per-session up ~12x.

asha: TL;DR: continuous batching regression + aggressive prefetch -> kv cache blowup for long prompts. Hosts run out of GPU RAM -> OOM. Customer impact: some hosted customers experience 5xx / session resets.

sanjay: Quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefetch to 0.1x 2) reduce batch_window to 5ms 3) enable kv eviction cap for in-flight sessions 4) roll back batcher rollout to v1 canary. Doing 1 and 2 now via runtime feature flags.

leo: Executing flag change (runtime API):
```
POST /runtime/v1/flags
{ "flag":"prefetch_scale", "value": 0.1 }
POST /runtime/v1/config
{ "config":"batch_window_ms", "value":5 }
```

maria: Applied. Observability: prefetch requests dropped ~85% within 30s, kv-map growth rate falling. OOM count decreasing but still seeing a tail of failures from already blown-up sessions.

support-bot: Logged customer impact — top affected: realtime-ai-prod, analytics-labs, chatflow-inc. CS pinged realtime-ai-prod (account id: acct-8271) and opened incident tickets with temporary workaround guidance.

asha: For the remaining tail we should forcibly evict stale prefix state for sessions exceeding 200k tokens. Proposing an emergency eviction job: `evict_sessions(token_count>200000)` and rate-limit to avoid causing mass disconnects.

leo: I ran a dry-run and counted ~1.2k sessions over threshold. Doing a graceful eviction with `max-evict-per-min=200` now.

sanjay: Also reverting the continuous-batching v2 rollout to previous stable on canary and pausing rollout. Revert command: `orbctl rollout revert continuous-batching v2 --to stable` (done).

eng-runtime-oncall: Taking handoff at 09:34 UTC. Current state: OOMs dropped from 58/m to 4/m; latency stable; errors 5xx down to 1.2%. Continuing: monitor for 30m, let eviction finish, then prepare a hotfix patch with hard caps in runtime.

maria: Hotfix notes for patch: 1) enforce per-session kv-entries upper bound (e.g., 250k entries) 2) prefetch should respect remaining GPU memory budget 3) add metric alert for kv-growth-rate per-session. Will draft PR.

leo: Quick config hotpatch applied for immediate protection:
```
# emergency runtime config
runtime.kvcache.max_entries_per_session = 250000
runtime.prefetch.global_scale = 0.1
runtime.batch.window_ms = 5
```
Applied via infra API: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/infra/apply -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d @hotpatch.json`

support-bot: Customer-facing note posted to #support-incident-updates: "We're mitigating an issue causing session resets for a subset of hosted customers. Engineers have throttled prefetch and reverted a recent batching rollout; we'll follow up with root cause and ETA for full fix."

asha: Remaining action items before Monday: - PR for runtime caps + graceful eviction logic - telemetry for per-session kv growth + per-deploy canary diff tests - postmortem and rollback playbook update.

eng-runtime-oncall: I'll own the follow-up. Next steps: collect heap dumps from two affected hosts (host-17, host-23), run offline analysis on worst offenders, and ship hotfix PR. Scheduling handoff to next oncall at 13:00 UTC.

sanjay: Incident summary for pagerduty: Cause = continuous-batching v2 + aggressive prefetch interacting badly with long-prompt workloads -> kv-cache growth -> OOMs. Mitigation = throttle prefetch, reduce batch window, enforce per-session caps, revert rollout. Customer impact = temporary increased 5xx for ~3% of requests for 40m window; major customers notified.

maria: Adding one note — network of long-prompt bursts came from an automated ingestion job in realtime-ai that changed its request size distribution; CS will coordinate with them on backpressure and request shaping.

support-bot: All action items captured in ticket INC2965432100-TO-ENG. Postmortem owner: eng-runtime (maria).

eng-runtime-oncall: Leaving a final log entry before off-shift: OOMs trending down, eviction job completed (1.1k sessions evicted over 5m), runtime caps applied. Will follow up with full RCA doc and timeline.

sanjay: Thanks everyone — great rapid coordination. If anything spikes again, re-open this thread or ping @pagerduty oncall. :thumbsup:
